reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07) because a change to billing import validation rules around August is causing bills to be issued incorrectly even on accounts with actual (non-estimated) meter reads, as shown by disputed bills skewing to ACTUAL read type (1785) over ESTIMATED (1240) (E-02). This rules out AMI-read delivery failure and field-manual-read handoff failure as the dominant mechanism (both contradicted by E-02), and rules out tariff change (E-01) and slow ticket response handling (E-03) as drivers.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07). Billing import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 and comparing raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads v4.2-firmware meters that report register values in 0.1 m3 units (E-14) as high-consumption, causing billing import to reject an otherwise validly-delivered AMI read (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and substitute an ESTIMATED bill instead; this accounts for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (E-12). This confirmed mechanism explains the ESTIMATED-read share of disputes (41% of 3025, E-02) but does not yet explain the majority of disputes that carry ACTUAL read type (1785 of 3025, E-02), whose cause remains open.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
